sources.outlet: Orin Kerr blog post (Volokh Conspiracy mirror on Goodreads)
sources.quote: According to the chart, the Fourth Circuit is the least likely to issue published opinions. Last year, only 7% of 4th Circuit opinions were published.
sources.searcher_note: Background only: 2009-2010 data, Fourth Circuit historically the lowest-publishing circuit; different window from the lead

notes: No news, trade-press or blog coverage found reporting a rise in Fourth Circuit published decisions in FY2025, the 375 count, the +25% figure, or the median circuit falling 17%. The only same-entity, same-window numbers are the courts' own Table B-12 (FY2025 and FY2019), which use a different definition (last opinion in cases terminated on the merits) from the lead's FJC/CourtListener counts. Quotes for B-12 are the Fourth Circuit table row as extracted from the PDF text; column order: total, by consolidation, last opinion total, oral, signed published, signed unpublished, reasoned unsigned published, reasoned unsigned unpublished, unsigned-without-comment published, unsigned-without-comment unpublished, percent unpublished. A CRS report (R48846, 2026-02-06) gives only all-circuit precedential totals (3,369 in FY2024), no per-circuit counts, so not recorded.
